analysis.title: Weekly Wrap: Multi-Strat Alpha & HF Returns Likely to Recover, but Uncertainty Persists
key_insights: JPM's Schlegel says risks outweighed tailwinds over the past two weeks versus the Oct 23, 2026 note. The risks named were deteriorating Eq L/S alpha, neutral CTAs who could still sell, and soft retail demand.

The note asks whether capitulation has occurred and whether market or HF alpha will rebound. It says history makes a rebound more likely than not, but the path is murky and upcoming market catalysts could still have a big impact.
The market does not equal HF alpha, and HF outcomes could vary by strategy going forward.

Multi-Strat pain may be easing. After several weeks of negative long-short spreads and the largest 20-day Multi-Strat de-grossing since Covid, L-S spreads improved last week. Tuesday and Thursday were positive, leaving 5-day alpha close to flat despite a weak Wednesday.

Multi-Strat 20-day gross flows first fell below the 5th percentile on Oct. 27. In 9 of 10 prior cases, alpha was higher over the following 20 days. Gross flows typically began to recover after about 10 days. The post-Covid episode was the main exception.

US HF de-grossing is now below its seasonal average, and gross flows have tended to move sideways from here. The pattern in past midterm election years most resembles 2022, when de-grossing continued into mid-month. Gross flows recovered in December in both comparison years, but that recovery coincided with a market sell-off and substantial short additions.

In the past five years, HFs rebounded over the following 5 and 10 days in all eight comparable events where 5- and 20-day net returns fell below -2z. Late February 2020 and late October 2018 were followed by further losses. A rebound in absolute HF returns may depend partly on the market.
Selling has not yet signaled broad capitulation. The broad net selling needed to push US TPM to a very negative four-week change has not appeared.

HF flows diverge by region. EMEA and China/HK saw net buying, while North America and Japan saw net selling, with North America sharply de-grossed. European short covering reached an extreme 3z level, last seen in late 2022.

HF net leverage fell about 4% over the past week, near 12-month lows. Eq L/S net leverage is at a three-year low. All Strategy net leverage remains higher, around the 40th percentile on a three-/five-year basis.

Global momentum exposure is near three-year lows and close to neutral. The 6m z-score of positioning and price is back near its summer lows, suggesting much of the move lower may have occurred for now. APAC momentum exposure has fallen quickly from more extreme levels.

In US themes, Semis remained the most net-sold, with positioning back near early-2026 levels. Software flows have been more neutral while positioning continues to recover. Broader AI-cyclical exposure has fallen quickly, while Defensives ex-Healthcare have begun to rebound.

Upcoming market catalysts are likely to have a big impact.

tension_points.bull_case: Multi-Strat L-S spreads improved last week and 5-day alpha is close to flat. In 9 of 10 prior de-grossing episodes alpha rose over the next 20 days. HFs rebounded in all eight comparable drawdowns of the past five years. Momentum exposure has reset near three-year lows.
tension_points.bear_case: Eq L/S alpha is still deteriorating, CTAs are neutral and could still sell, and retail demand is soft. Late February 2020 and late October 2018 saw further losses after similar drawdowns. The midterm-year pattern resembles 2022, when de-grossing continued into mid-month and the December recovery coincided with a market sell-off.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Broad net selling that pushes US TPM to a very negative four-week change, which would signal capitulation had not yet occurred or was still under way.
